title: Postman environment export: secret variable with an empty value and a source object
summary: A synthetic Postman environment export with one entry named postman_api_key, type secret, an empty value, and a source object naming provider postman, a local vault type, and synthetic secretId and vaultId strings. The entry has the same label and type as a secret that holds a value but carries no value.
rationale: The label, the type and the identifier-like strings all read like credential material, and the key name is the strongest possible signal. The SDK describes the source object as metadata on how to resolve the value from an external source, so the entry is a pointer: the credential lives in the vault and not in the file. This is the structured-object form of a secret-manager pointer, distinct from an inline double-brace reference. Whether the identifiers of a real source object are confidential is not documented in the sources read, so the fixture uses only obviously synthetic ids and the expectation does not extend to real ones.

expectation.rationale: No span. The SDK documents a variable definition with an empty value and a source object as the way a secret variable is resolved from a vault, and describes the source object as metadata on how to resolve the value from an external source. No secret byte is present in this input. Preconditions: exported JSON text read as UTF-8; no vault resolution is performed or assumed. The expectation is limited to the synthetic ids in the fixture.

sources.supports: Documented example of a secret variable resolved from the Postman local vault: type secret, empty value, a source object with provider postman and secretId and vaultId properties; the source property carries metadata on how to resolve the value from an external source.

notes: Project-authored by the Redact Secret project, which maintains this repository; not independent evidence. Draft; not yet reviewed. Authored from the cited page read on 2026-10-04; no scanner was run. Origin: evidence-derived from the SDK's documented example, synthetic ids. The sensitivity of the identifiers in a real source object is unresolved.
